reviews.title: Not Worth the $$
reviews.text:
I’ve been playing this game for about 2 years and I grow continuously more disappointed for a few reasons.

As your server ages, the power imbalance grows between people who play casually and people who spend tens of thousands (literally).

The game has a set of templates for events. New events are typically just dupes of old events.

The gacha system is awful. You have a 0.1% chance of getting an event character and that % doesn’t change the more you pull until you hit hard pity. My rate of success is lower in this game than any other gacha I’ve played. Because the % chance of a good pull is so low, the only way to really succeed is to spend $100s per event. The devs could make the new characters more accessible and the whales would still vastly outpace the rest of us. The devs just want to make it that much clearer which players they value and which they don’t.

I’ve stopped spending because it just doesn’t seem worth it compared to what I can get in other games for the same price. Other games I’ve played give you voice acting, animated interactive videos, and a plot that evolves over time. I’d have already stopped playing but for the connection I have with a few other players.

reviews.title: Hidden Pay Walls
reviews.text:
I would have rated this game higher because the art and collabs are really good.  

However, during each collab and event, the ability to get tickets to pull multiple characters disappears.  Then the only way to gain tickets to pull for characters in the specific collabs are hidden behind paywalls.  To get 50 pulls you then need to pay $99.99.  But the requirement for a guaranteed pull is just under $200.

For example, the demonslayer collab had 4 characters you could pull for.  To get them guaranteed, you would have to spend $800 based on their options.  This means you don’t really get to enjoy the gacha part of the collabs.  This is common place across all the collabs and events.

reviews.title: This game only cares about the rich
reviews.text: I started playing this game for the relaxing "slow life" vibe, but it has become an incredibly frustrating, pay-to-win experience.The monetization is completely unbalanced. There are countless event characters that I have missed out on simply because they are locked behind massive paywalls. On top of that, the luck and drop rates for free-to-play resources are incredibly unforgiving. If you do not spend significant amounts of real money, you are completely locked out of the core progression and the most exciting rewards.The developers care more about catering to high spenders than making the game fair or enjoyable for the regular community. For a game marketed as a casual experience, it shouldn't feel like you are being penalized or called poor just because you choose not to open your wallet.Please balance the event drop rates and make characters actually obtainable through dedicated gameplay, not just credit cards. I apologize if I sound rude, I’m just very frustrated and upset by this issue and I feel like the devs and game is calling me poor. I love the game, truly, but maybe tone down this nonsense?

reviews.title: My honest review from when I played the game years ago
reviews.text: I played this game years ago on a different device, and I remember liking some characters, but none of them were the ones categorized under the family tag. Instead, I was more interested in the male NPCs that fall under the follower tag. I mention this because I find the female characters rather boring; they lack any real substance, which is why I stopped playing. This sentiment also applies to the male characters that fall under the family tag. I can’t see why I should be more interested in NPCs that can be part of my family, especially when characters who can join the family should just be ordinary NPCs. I will reconsider my review and rating if there’s ever an update allowing non-family NPCs—both male and female—to be part of your family. Edit: I revised my previous review, and I was even more certain; the NPC followers are more desirable for joining your family than the characters who can actually become family members.
